$comment: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 ComradeArt. SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. One installed-system scenario definition. Scenarios are data, not code, so that changing what a scenario means is a reviewable edit that bumps scenarioVersion and stales prior evidence — never a silent drift inside a runner script.
title: Bunny OS installed-system scenario definition

name.$comment: Slug form so the name embeds directly into an ISQ evidence identifier without transformation.

environment.$comment: const, not enum: this schema version only defines VM scenarios. Physical scenarios need a hardware record binding this schema has no fields for, and widening the enum before those fields exist would invite physical claims with VM-shaped evidence.

preExistingData.$comment: blank and preExistingData are both explicit because 'blank: false' alone does not say whether the non-blank content is meant to survive; a preservation scenario and an overwrite scenario differ exactly here.

tpm.$comment: swtpm exercises the code path only; evidence produced under it records tpmState swtpm and never satisfies a physical-TPM requirement.

network.$comment: absent means no NIC at all, not an unplugged one — offline scenarios must be structurally offline so a runner cannot quietly fetch anything.

digestField.$comment: Names the evidence-context field that pins this medium (e.g. installationArtifactDigest). The scenario never carries a digest of its own: the context is the single authority, and a scenario with its own digest would be a second one.

timeoutSeconds.$comment: A hit timeout is a FAIL, never a retry-until-green; retrying converts a flaky behaviour into a pass without anyone deciding to.

required.$comment: A required marker that never appears fails the scenario; an optional one is recorded either way so its absence stays visible.

expectedOutcome.$comment: Some scenarios EXPECT refusal — a wrong-credential unlock must fail, and the scenario passes qualification only when it does. Encoding the expectation here keeps 'the installer refused' distinguishable from 'the scenario broke'.

destructive.$comment: True when the scenario intentionally destroys disk content; a runner must refuse to point a destructive scenario at anything but scratch media.
